papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a broadly useful and adaptable family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and NLP, KD methods extend beyond soft-target matching to include internal-representation transfer, multi-teacher and teacher-engineering strategies, adversarial and contrastive objectives, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. Practical success depends on matching what is transferred and how it is transferred to student capacity, task properties, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central and Complementary Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a practical, versatile, and central approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones across vision and NLP. KD can transfer outputs, internal representations, and structure from teacher to student, and—when combined with task-aware selection, adaptive teacher schedules, or structured pruning—yields strong trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and robustness. However, KD has limits tied to teacher–student capacity gaps, data and compute requirements, and potential optimization mismatches; these limits motivate hybrid pipelines and careful design choices that match what is distilled to the student’s capacity and the target application.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical design space for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller students so that compact models approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. The literature documents many distinct signals (soft outputs, hidden states, attention and feature correlations), coupling strategies (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, curriculum schedules), and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or module replacement. Success depends on choosing what to transfer to match student capacity and task needs, managing teacher–student gaps and data availability, and integrating robustness and latency considerations. Empirical work across classification, generation, retrieval, continual learning, and reinforcement learning shows KD is indispensable for many compression problems but must be applied task-awarely and often in combination with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: On Learning the Geodesic Path for Incremental Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Neural networks notoriously suffer from the problem of catastrophic forgetting, the phenomenon of forgetting the past knowledge when acquiring new knowledge. Overcoming catastrophic forgetting is of significant importance to emulate the process of "incremental learning", where the model is capable of learning from sequential experience in an efficient and robust way. State-of-the-art techniques for incremental learning make use of knowledge distillation towards preventing catastrophic forgetting. Therein, one updates the network while ensuring that the network's responses to previously seen concepts remain stable throughout updates. This in practice is done by minimizing the dissimilarity between current and previous responses of the network one way or another. Our work contributes a novel method to the arsenal of distillation techniques. In contrast to the previous state of the art, we propose to firstly construct low-dimensional manifolds for previous and current responses and minimize the dissimilarity between the responses along the geodesic connecting the manifolds. This induces a more formidable knowledge distillation with smooth properties which preserves the past knowledge more efficiently as observed by our comprehensive empirical study.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and NLP, KD encompasses soft-label matching, intermediate-representation alignment, adversarial/contrastive objectives, and progressive or hybrid compression pipelines; when matched to student capacity and task constraints and combined with complementary methods (e.g., pruning or module replacement) it yields strong trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and memory. Remaining challenges include reliably transferring robustness, selecting task-relevant internal signals, and reducing dependence on large unlabeled corpora or heavy distillation compute.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Mechanisms, Variants, Task Considerations, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring useful information from teacher models. Over the past decade KD has diversified from simple soft-target matching into a rich set of methods that transfer logits, intermediate representations, feature correlations, and decision-boundary information; use single, multiple, evolving, or learned teachers; and combine with pruning or module replacement. Practical success depends on aligning what is transferred to student capacity and task requirements, and best results typically come from hybrid, task-aware strategies that match distillation signals to model and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a diverse and practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large models (teachers) to smaller models (students) to achieve deployable efficiency while preserving performance. The literature spans soft-target (logit) transfer, internal- and layer-wise representation matching, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online/evolving teacher schedules, self-distillation, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with structured pruning or module replacement. Empirical results across vision and a wide range of NLP tasks (classification, ranking, summarization, translation, dense retrieval) show that no single recipe suffices: success depends on the choice of distilled signal, teacher–student capacity gap, task complexity, and data availability. Practical deployments therefore treat distillation as a toolbox of complementary methods whose components should be selected and combined according to task and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Remains Central for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Principles, Variants, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured from a simple teacher-to-student soft-label transfer into a rich family of methods that target robustness, internal representation alignment, task-specific selection of signals, and efficient compression pipelines. Across vision, language, and sequence generation tasks, distillation enables compact models to retain or approach the performance of large models while enabling practical latency and memory benefits. Effective distillation designs combine multiple signals (logits, hidden states, feature correlations), adapt the teacher-student relationship during training, and can be integrated with pruning or module-replacement strategies to achieve strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Toolbox: Task-Aware, Hybrid Strategies for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students, but its success hinges on matching the distillation strategy to task demands, student capacity, and data constraints. Rather than a single recipe, KD should be treated as a flexible toolbox combining soft-labels, internal-representation alignment, teacher adaptation, layer-wise filtering, adversarial objectives, and pruning or module-replacement where appropriate. When chosen and combined thoughtfully—exposing informative internal signals, adapting teacher supervision to student capacity, and using task-aware selection—KD yields compact models that retain high performance, robustness, and practical latency gains.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models by transferring useful predictive behavior and internal structure from teacher models to smaller students. The field encompasses a wide spectrum of techniques — matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, layer-wise or module replacement, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher strategies, and combinations with structured pruning — each suited to different capacity gaps, data regimes, latency constraints, and robustness needs. Empirical and theoretical work shows distillation helps by smoothing supervision, reducing data complexity, shaping per-instance gradients and decision boundaries, and providing representational priors that smaller models can exploit. Effective compression typically requires choosing or adapting what is transferred to the student's capacity and the target task, and often benefits from hybrid strategies (e.g., distillation plus pruning or progressive replacement).

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single algorithm but as a flexible, task-aware toolbox that reliably compresses large models into smaller, deployable students when signals and schedules are matched to student capacity and task needs. Combining soft-target transfer with representation-level alignment, teacher engineering (multi- and online-teacher schemes, self-distillation), adversarial or contrastive objectives, and hybrid pipelines that integrate pruning or progressive module replacement produces the strongest empirical trade-offs among accuracy, latency, memory, and robustness. Important caveats remain — notably teacher–student capacity gaps, data and compute demands, and imperfect robustness transfer — which motivate careful choice of what to transfer and when and the selective use of complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques seek to transfer useful predictive behavior from larger, high-capacity models (teachers) into smaller, faster models (students) while preserving accuracy and often adding desirable properties such as robustness or task-specific efficiency. A wide range of methods has been developed: soft-label distillation, internal-representation matching, layer- or module-wise compression, adversarial and contrastive objectives, online and multi-teacher schemes, and hybrid approaches that combine pruning with distillation. Empirical results across vision, language, ranking, summarization, and reinforcement learning show that carefully chosen distillation strategies can reclaim much of a teacher's performance in a compact student, but outcomes depend strongly on the choice of distilled signals, the alignment of capacities, teacher selection or adaptation, and task-specific constraints. Recent work also emphasizes robustness transfer, task-aware filtering of teacher signals, and alternatives to distillation such as structured pruning that can match distillation in latency without extra unlabeled data. Remaining challenges include principled selection of which teacher knowledge to transfer, scaling to diverse prediction tasks, and combining distillation with compression and robustness objectives in a computationally efficient way.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware Hybrid Toolbox for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is most effective when treated not as a single recipe but as a task-aware, hybrid toolbox: designers should select which teacher signals to transfer (logits, intermediate representations, attention/feature maps, or training dynamics), adapt teacher supervision to student capacity, and combine distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, progressive module replacement, or module-substitution schedules). When these design choices are matched to task constraints and data availability, distilled students can approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and robustness requirements. Remaining challenges include reliably transferring robustness, selecting task-relevant internal signals, and closing large teacher–student capacity gaps without overconstraining the student.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware Hybrid Toolbox: Central Role and Practical Limits in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applicable family of methods for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When treated as a task-aware, hybrid toolbox—selecting which teacher signals to transfer (logits, hidden states, attention or feature correlations), adapting teacher supervision to student capacity, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques such as structured pruning or progressive module replacement—KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency and memory constraints. However, KD is not a universal panacea: its effectiveness depends on task complexity, teacher–student capacity gaps, availability of data, and the choice of transferred signals, and in some deployment regimes simpler compression-first strategies can be preferable. Practical adoption therefore requires careful teacher engineering, signal selection, and integration with other compression methods to balance accuracy, latency, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and How to Use It
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and flexible route to producing compact, high-performance models for deep learning and NLP. When matched to task requirements and student capacity and when combined with complementary compression strategies, distillation routinely yields models that approach the accuracy of large teachers while delivering meaningful latency and memory gains. However, distillation is not universally superior: its benefits depend on what form of knowledge is transferred, the availability and complexity of training data, and the desired properties (e.g., robustness, latency). I argue that distillation should be treated as an indispensable component of a compression toolbox — applied with representation-level signals, teacher-aware adaptations, and hybridization with pruning or progressive replacement when appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible set of methods for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with task awareness — selecting what to transfer, adapting teacher signals to student capacity, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques — distillation routinely yields compact models that recover much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and robustness constraints. Practical success depends on careful design choices (what to match, how to adapt teachers, and whether to incorporate pruning or progressive replacement) rather than a single canonical recipe.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques aim to transfer performance from larger, high-capacity models to smaller, more efficient models for deployment or specialized use. Approaches span logit-based soft-label distillation, intermediate representation and layer-wise matching, teacher design and selection strategies, online/evolutionary teachers, curriculum or route-based supervision, and combinations with pruning and adversarial methods. In NLP, distillation has been adapted to pretrained transformers via progressive module replacement, layer-wise and task-aware filters, and by leveraging distilled data (pseudo-labeling) or parameter shrinking. Trade-offs include reliance on unlabeled data, teacher-student capacity gaps, and robustness concerns; recent work addresses these via teacher adaptation, confidence-weighting, and distillation objectives targeting representation geometry and decision boundaries.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Indispensable, Task-Aware Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a flexible, task-aware toolbox rather than a single algorithm. When designed to match what is transferred (logits, internal representations, attention or feature correlations) and how teachers and students are coupled (teacher engineering, online or multi-teacher schemes, curriculum or route-based schedules), KD routinely produces compact models that approach the performance of large teachers while meeting real-world latency, memory, and robustness requirements. The most reliable practice combines representation-focused distillation with teacher adaptation and, when necessary, complementary compression techniques such as structured pruning or progressive module replacement to address severe latency or data constraints.

Empirical results show KD routinely improves compact-model performance across vision, language, ranking, generation, and reinforcement learning when its components are chosen to match student capacity, task constraints, and data availability; remaining challenges include reliably transferring robustness, reducing data and compute costs of distillation, and selecting task-relevant intermediate signals.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster ones by transferring useful information from teacher models to students. Methods span matching teacher output distributions (soft labels), aligning internal representations at various granularities, adversarial and contrastive objectives, progressive module replacement, and task-aware or curriculum-based strategies. Distillation is used both for deployment-efficient models and as a tool in related problems (e.g., continual learning, pruning, robustness, retrieval, and task transfer). Empirical and theoretical work shows that what is transferred (e.g., global/class relations, instance-level difficulty signals, intermediate features) and how it is transferred (e.g., offline vs online, multi-teacher weighting, attention/feature matching, adversarial objectives) critically affect student performance. Practical trade-offs include compute and data requirements, robustness transfer, and the relative roles of pruning and distillation; newer work emphasizes making teacher signals more student-friendly and selecting or filtering teacher knowledge to match student capacity and the downstream task.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and empirically validated family of methods for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones. When treated as a toolbox—covering soft-label transfer, intermediate-representation matching, multi-teacher schedules, adversarial and contrastive objectives, and integrations with pruning or module replacement—KD reliably reduces model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, adapting teacher dynamics, and accounting for data and robustness constraints. KD is indispensable for many practical deployments, but practitioners should combine it with complementary compression strategies and task-aware design to navigate limits posed by capacity gaps, data scarcity, and robustness requirements.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Indispensable, Task-Aware Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is best understood not as a single algorithm but as a flexible, task-aware toolbox that, when designed to match what is transferred to student capacity and combined with complementary compression techniques, routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Its mechanisms include soft-target (logit) transfer, intermediate-representation alignment, attention and feature-correlation matching, teacher scheduling (offline, online, multi- or evolving teachers), and adversarial or contrastive objectives. Practical success requires adapting teacher signals to task and data constraints and recognizing limitations such as teacher–student capacity gaps, data requirements, and robustness transfer challenges.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques form a broad, practical toolkit for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. The literature shows many complementary algorithmic families — soft-target (logit) transfer, internal-representation and attention/feature matching, contrastive and adversarial objectives, progressive module replacement, multi- and online-teacher schedules, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with structured pruning or module replacement. Empirical work across vision, NLP, summarization, retrieval, and reinforcement learning indicates that no single recipe dominates: careful matching of what is distilled to student capacity and task needs, adapting teacher signals, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods tend to give the best accuracy–latency–size trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Flexible Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a core technique for compressing large models into efficient students for both vision and language tasks. A wide variety of KD formulations — from soft-label transfer and layer-wise matching to adversarial, online, and self-distillation — have demonstrated consistent gains in accuracy, inference speed, and memory footprint. However, distillation is not a single recipe: its effectiveness depends on teacher-student capacity gaps, the form of transferred information (logits, internal representations, attention maps), task characteristics, and data availability. Recent work shows that combining distillation with task-aware filtering, structured pruning, or teacher adaptation yields the best practical tradeoffs. Going forward, hybrid and task-aware distillation strategies that explicitly align representation, decision-boundary, and robustness objectives promise the most reliable compression outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, task-aware approach for transferring behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has expanded well beyond simple soft-label matching into a rich toolbox that includes logits transfer, intermediate-representation and attention matching, adversarial and contrastive objectives, meta- and online-teacher schemes, progressive module replacement, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with structured pruning. When chosen and combined according to student capacity, task demands, and deployment constraints, KD routinely improves compact-model performance; however, open challenges remain in reliably transferring robustness, managing teacher–student capacity gaps, and reducing heavy data or compute needs for distillation.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible set of techniques that transfer information from larger teacher models into smaller student models to achieve deployable trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and robustness. Rather than a single recipe, KD comprises response-based, representation-based, adversarial, and meta- or multi-teacher methods that should be chosen and combined according to student capacity, task demands, and available data. When designed with task-aware choices of transferred signals and combined with complementary compression methods (e.g., structured pruning or progressive module replacement), distillation routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance; however, success requires careful management of teacher–student mismatch, data requirements, and robustness transfer.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and its Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning based models are relatively large, and it is hard to deploy such models on resource-limited devices such as mobile phones and embedded devices. One possible solution is knowledge distillation whereby a smaller model (student model) is trained by utilizing the information from a larger model (teacher model). In this paper, we present a survey of knowledge distillation techniques applied to deep learning models. To compare the performances of different techniques, we propose a new metric called distillation metric. Distillation metric compares different knowledge distillation algorithms based on sizes and accuracy scores. Based on the survey, some interesting conclusions are drawn and presented in this paper.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware Hybrid Toolbox for Reliable Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated not as a single algorithm but as a flexible, task-aware toolbox. Practical compression succeeds when designers choose which teacher signals to transfer (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention or feature statistics), adapt or engineer teachers to student capacity (single, multi-, evolving, or student-friendly teachers), and combine distillation with complementary compression techniques such as structured pruning or progressive module replacement. While KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance and improve latency and memory, open challenges remain in reliably transferring robustness, selecting task-relevant intermediate signals, and closing large teacher–student capacity gaps.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques form a rich set of methods to transfer information from larger "teacher" models to smaller "student" models or to produce compact models via pruning and module replacement. Approaches vary from matching soft targets to aligning internal representations, using adversarial objectives, contrastive or Wasserstein-based objectives, layer-wise and task-aware filters, and online or evolutionary teacher schedules. These techniques have been applied across domains including natural language understanding, summarization, machine translation, ranking, vision tasks, reinforcement learning, and incremental learning. Empirical work highlights that the benefits of distillation depend on teacher-student capacity gaps, what kind of knowledge is transferred (global label structure, domain priors, instance-specific signals), and data complexity; combining distillation with structured pruning or careful teacher selection often yields practical gains in latency and storage while preserving accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques aim to transfer performance from larger, high-capacity models to smaller, more efficient models for deployment or specialized use. Approaches span logit-based soft-label distillation, intermediate representation and layer-wise matching, teacher design and selection strategies, online/evolutionary teachers, curriculum or route-based supervision, and combinations with pruning and adversarial methods. In NLP, distillation has been adapted to pretrained transformers via progressive module replacement, layer-wise and task-aware filters, and by leveraging distilled data (pseudo-labeling) or parameter shrinking. Trade-offs include reliance on unlabeled data, teacher-student capacity gaps, and robustness concerns; recent work addresses these via teacher adaptation, confidence-weighting, and distillation objectives targeting representation geometry and decision boundaries.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models or produce compact subnetworks via pruning and module replacement. The literature has grown into a design space of methods that transfer final outputs (soft logits), internal representations (feature maps, attention, layer activations), or training dynamics (curricula, evolving teachers), and which operate in offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, and progressive-replacement regimes. Empirical and analytical work shows that success depends on matching the distilled information to student capacity and task demands, combining complementary compression tools (e.g., pruning or module replacement) when appropriate, and addressing practical constraints such as unlabeled-data needs, robustness transfer, and optimization stability. Effective distillation usually involves exposing informative internal signals, adapting teacher supervision to the student, and selecting task-relevant knowledge rather than naively copying all teacher behavior.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques form a broad, practical toolkit for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. The literature shows many complementary algorithmic families — soft-target (logit) transfer, internal-representation and attention/feature matching, contrastive and adversarial objectives, progressive module replacement, multi- and online-teacher schedules, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with structured pruning or module replacement. Empirical work across vision, NLP, summarization, retrieval, and reinforcement learning indicates that no single recipe dominates: careful matching of what is distilled to student capacity and task needs, adapting teacher signals, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods tend to give the best accuracy–latency–size trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, task-aware approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a broad design space that includes intermediate-representation alignment, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher schemes, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. Practical success depends on selecting appropriate transfer signals for the student’s capacity, adapting teacher signals during training, and combining KD with complementary compression tools to satisfy constraints on latency, data, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a flexible family of techniques for transferring the behavior and internal structure of large models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD evolved from soft-label matching into a broad design space that includes logits transfer, layer- and feature-wise alignment, attention or correlation matching, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher schemes, and progressive module replacement. Practical success is task- and capacity-aware: practitioners must choose what to transfer, adapt teacher signals to student capacity, and often combine distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, module replacement, or shrink-and-fine-tune) to meet latency, memory, and robustness constraints. While KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance in many vision and NLP tasks, its effectiveness depends on data complexity, teacher–student gaps, and the choice of transferred signals, and alternative or hybrid pipelines can be preferable in some regimes.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a broad, practical family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Across vision and NLP, KD variants transfer information ranging from final soft-labels to intermediate representations, attention maps, and structured feature correlations; practitioners routinely combine distillation with complementary compression methods (e.g., structured pruning or progressive module replacement) and adapt teacher signals to student capacity and task demands. Empirical and theoretical work identifies multiple mechanisms for KD’s effectiveness — better optimization trajectories, regularization-like effects, richer concept learning, and per-instance gradient shaping — while also highlighting important practical factors such as teacher–student capacity gap, the availability of unlabeled data, and robustness transfer. Open problems include reliably selecting task-relevant signals to transfer, minimizing unnecessary constraints from mismatched teachers, and integrating distillation with pruning or architectural changes to maximize latency and accuracy tradeoffs.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central and Complementary Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a versatile and effective approach for compressing large models into compact, deployable students across vision and NLP. KD’s strengths arise from its ability to transfer soft targets, internal representations, and task-relevant signals to reshape student training dynamics, and it admits many practical variants (multi-teacher, adversarial, curriculum, online/evolutionary, and progressive replacement). At the same time, structured pruning and module-replacement methods can be competitive or complementary when latency, data, or compute constraints dominate. Best practice is a toolbox mentality: choose what to transfer to match student capacity, adapt the teacher–student relationship during training, and combine distillation with pruning or curriculum strategies when appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for producing compact, deployable deep models that often preserve much of the accuracy of larger teachers. KD succeeds by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate structure, but its effectiveness depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity, the target task, and data constraints. Best practical outcomes arise from treating distillation as a flexible, task-aware toolbox — exposing internal representations as well as logits, adapting teachers and schedules, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques such as structured pruning or progressive module replacement. KD is indispensable in many pipelines but not universally optimal; careful design and hybridization are required to reach reliable accuracy–latency–robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Student Network Learning via Evolutionary Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation provides an effective way to transfer knowledge via teacher-student learning, where most existing distillation approaches apply a fixed pre-trained model as teacher to supervise the learning of student network. This manner usually brings in a big capability gap between teacher and student networks during learning. Recent researches have observed that a small teacher-student capability gap can facilitate knowledge transfer. Inspired by that, we propose an evolutionary knowledge distillation approach to improve the transfer effectiveness of teacher knowledge. Instead of a fixed pre-trained teacher, an evolutionary teacher is learned online and consistently transfers intermediate knowledge to supervise student network learning on-the-fly. To enhance intermediate knowledge representation and mimicking, several simple guided modules are introduced between corresponding teacher-student blocks. In this way, the student can simultaneously obtain rich internal knowledge and capture its growth process, leading to effective student network learning. Extensive experiments clearly demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach as well as good adaptability in the low-resolution and few-sample visual recognition scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central and Complementary Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a practical, versatile, and central approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones across vision and NLP. KD can transfer outputs, internal representations, and structure from teacher to student, and—when combined with task-aware selection, adaptive teacher schedules, or structured pruning—yields strong trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and robustness. However, KD has limits tied to teacher–student capacity gaps, data and compute requirements, and potential optimization mismatches; these limits motivate hybrid pipelines and careful design choices that match what is distilled to the student’s capacity and the target application.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware, Hybrid Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a central, versatile technique for producing compact, high-performing models in deep learning and NLP. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD succeeds by transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, and structured behaviors from teachers to students, but no single KD recipe dominates all settings. The most reliable practical approach is hybrid and task-aware: expose informative internal representations, adapt teacher signals to student capacity and the target task, and combine distillation with complementary compression methods such as structured pruning, progressive module replacement, or targeted robustness procedures to meet latency, memory, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Hybrid Toolbox for Reliable Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is most effective when treated as a flexible, task-aware toolbox rather than a single algorithm. Practical compression succeeds by (1) exposing and aligning informative internal representations, (2) adapting teacher signals to student capacity and task requirements, and (3) combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (e.g., structured pruning or progressive module replacement) when latency, memory, or robustness constraints demand it. With these design patterns, distillation routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world deployment constraints, though limits remain when data is scarce or teacher–student gaps are large.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques produce compact models that retain much of the performance of large networks by transferring knowledge from one or more teacher models to a student. Research over the last decade has diversified the KD toolkit beyond soft-label supervision to include internal representation matching, adversarial objectives, contrastive and Wasserstein distances, progressive module replacement, online and multi-teacher schemes, teacher-training strategies, and task-aware filter selection. These approaches have been applied across computer vision, NLP (including pretrained Transformers and summarization), retrieval, detection, reinforcement learning, and continual learning. Practical trade-offs arise from teacher-student capacity gaps, data requirements, optimization difficulties, and robustness concerns; contemporary work addresses these by narrowing capability gaps (e.g., evolving or student-friendly teachers), selecting or weighting teacher signals, and distilling only task-relevant intermediate features. Empirical studies show that no single KD recipe dominates all settings: the best choice depends on model architectures, target tasks, and constraints on data, latency, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware Hybrid Toolbox for Reliable Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and practical approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. Rather than a single recipe, KD comprises a toolbox of techniques — soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi- and evolving-teacher schedules, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or module replacement. Its success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity and task constraints, engineering teacher supervision to be student-friendly, and choosing complementary compression methods when latency, data, or robustness demands require them. While KD is often indispensable for deployment, alternative or hybrid strategies (structured pruning, shrink-and-fine-tune) can be competitive in constrained regimes.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching into a rich design space that includes logits and temperature tuning, alignment of intermediate representations and attention maps, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher schedules, self-distillation, and progressive module-replacement pipelines. Empirical work across computer vision, language understanding, translation, summarization, retrieval, and reinforcement learning shows KD often substantially narrows the performance gap between teacher and student while improving latency and memory usage; however, success depends on matching what and how information is transferred to student capacity, task constraints, and available data. Complementary methods (structured pruning, module replacement, and teacher adaptation) and task-aware choices usually yield the most reliable compression outcomes. Remaining challenges include reliably transferring robustness, handling teacher–student capacity gaps, choosing task-relevant intermediate signals, and reducing dependence on large unlabeled corpora.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple soft-label matching into a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-representation alignment, multi- and online-teacher schemes, adversarial and contrastive objectives, curriculum- and task-aware schedules, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. Practical success typically depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity and task constraints, adapting or selecting teacher signals to be student-friendly, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods when latency, data, or robustness demands require it. Remaining challenges include reliably transferring robustness, minimizing teacher–student mismatch, and reducing the data and compute overhead of effective distillation.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Methods and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques aim to transfer the functional behavior of large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, or otherwise more practical models. The literature has developed a range of strategies — from soft-target distillation and internal-representation matching to adversarial, contrastive, and progressive replacement approaches — and has explored applications across classification, vision, retrieval, summarization, machine translation, and incremental learning. Practical considerations that influence success include teacher–student capacity gap, the choice of distillation target (logits, intermediate features, or decision-boundary samples), availability of unlabeled data, and the goal of robustness or latency reduction. Empirical work shows that carefully chosen or adapted distillation techniques can approach teacher performance while delivering large reductions in size or latency; complementary approaches such as structured pruning can yield further speedups or remove the need for extra unlabeled data.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Towards Effective and Robust Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Distillation-Centric Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile and empirically powerful tool for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students. I argue that the most reliable path to high-quality compressed models in both vision and NLP is a hybrid approach that (1) emphasizes internal-representation and layer-wise distillation for transferring structured task-relevant knowledge, (2) uses task-aware selection and teacher-selection strategies to reduce irrelevant signal, (3) integrates adversarial and robustness-aware techniques when robustness matters, and (4) combines distillation with structured pruning or progressive module replacement when latency and memory constraints dominate. This position synthesizes empirical and theoretical findings across distillation, multi-teacher strategies, robustness, and pruning to recommend practical design patterns for model compression.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware Hybrid Toolbox: Central Role and Practical Limits in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applicable family of methods for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When treated as a task-aware, hybrid toolbox—selecting which teacher signals to transfer (logits, hidden states, attention or feature correlations), adapting teacher supervision to student capacity, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques such as structured pruning or progressive module replacement—KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency and memory constraints. However, KD is not a universal panacea: its effectiveness depends on task complexity, teacher–student capacity gaps, availability of data, and the choice of transferred signals, and in some deployment regimes simpler compression-first strategies can be preferable. Practical adoption therefore requires careful teacher engineering, signal selection, and integration with other compression methods to balance accuracy, latency, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of techniques for transferring information from larger or ensemble models into smaller models to improve compact model quality and efficiency. Across vision, language, retrieval, and sequential decision-making, KD variants include soft-label distillation, internal-representation matching, layer-wise and module-replacement strategies, adversarial and contrastive formulations, multi-teacher and teacher-selection methods, online/evolutionary teacher schedules, and task-aware distillation that selects which teacher knowledge to transfer. KD has been combined with structured pruning and other compression approaches to achieve substantial speedups while preserving accuracy. Practical challenges include the teacher–student capacity gap, internal representation mismatch, the need for unlabeled data in some pipelines, and retaining robustness or previously learned knowledge in incremental settings. A range of remedies have been proposed: learning student-friendly or adaptive teachers, matching internal feature statistics, confidence-aware weighting, adversarial and contrastive objectives, progressive module replacement, and task-aware layer filters. In practice, distillation has enabled state-of-the-art trade-offs in NLP tasks (classification, summarization, retrieval, machine translation, and non-autoregressive generation), vision tasks, and reinforcement learning, while also being adapted for adversarial robustness and continual learning.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Over the last decade the field has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a rich design space that includes logits and intermediate-representation transfer, contrastive and adversarial objectives, multi- and online-teacher schedules, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. Practical application is task- and capacity-aware: success depends on choosing what to transfer, adapting teacher signals to student capacity and data availability, and combining distillation with complementary compression tools where appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a broadly useful and adaptable family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and NLP, KD methods extend beyond soft-target matching to include internal-representation transfer, multi-teacher and teacher-engineering strategies, adversarial and contrastive objectives, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or progressive module replacement. Practical success depends on matching what is transferred and how it is transferred to student capacity, task properties, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically central approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in both vision and NLP. The literature shows KD is not a single recipe but a design space of techniques (logits, internal representations, adversarial/contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online schedules) that, when matched to student capacity and task demands and combined with complementary compression methods (e.g., structured pruning or progressive module replacement), yield strong trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and robustness. Effective practice requires selecting what to transfer, adapting teacher signals to the student, and hybridizing distillation with pruning or architecture-aware replacement where appropriate; remaining challenges include reliably transferring robustness, choosing task-relevant intermediate signals, and managing teacher–student mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Indispensable, Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from matching soft logits into a comprehensive toolbox that transfers output behavior, intermediate representations, and training dynamics from larger teachers to compact students. When chosen and combined with attention to student capacity, task constraints, and complementary compression techniques, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. However, its practical success depends on matching the form of transferred knowledge to the student and task, managing teacher–student capacity gaps, and addressing robustness and data constraints; in some settings, hybrid pipelines or alternative compression methods may be preferable or necessary.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical design space for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller students so that compact models approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. The literature documents many distinct signals (soft outputs, hidden states, attention and feature correlations), coupling strategies (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, curriculum schedules), and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning or module replacement. Success depends on choosing what to transfer to match student capacity and task needs, managing teacher–student gaps and data availability, and integrating robustness and latency considerations. Empirical work across classification, generation, retrieval, continual learning, and reinforcement learning shows KD is indispensable for many compression problems but must be applied task-awarely and often in combination with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) is a model-agnostic technique to improve model quality while having a fixed capacity budget. It is a commonly used technique for model compression, where a larger capacity teacher model with better quality is used to train a more compact student model with better inference efficiency. Through distillation, one hopes to benefit from student's compactness, without sacrificing too much on model quality. Despite the large success of knowledge distillation, better understanding of how it benefits student model's training dynamics remains under-explored. In this paper, we categorize teacher's knowledge into three hierarchical levels and study its effects on knowledge distillation: (1) knowledge of the `universe', where KD brings a regularization effect through label smoothing; (2) domain knowledge, where teacher injects class relationships prior to student's logit layer geometry; and (3) instance specific knowledge, where teacher rescales student model's per-instance gradients based on its measurement on the event difficulty. Using systematic analyses and extensive empirical studies on both synthetic and real-world datasets, we confirm that the aforementioned three factors play a major role in knowledge distillation. Furthermore, based on our findings, we diagnose some of the failure cases of applying KD from recent studies.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Remains Central for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Principles, Variants, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured from a simple teacher-to-student soft-label transfer into a rich family of methods that target robustness, internal representation alignment, task-specific selection of signals, and efficient compression pipelines. Across vision, language, and sequence generation tasks, distillation enables compact models to retain or approach the performance of large models while enabling practical latency and memory benefits. Effective distillation designs combine multiple signals (logits, hidden states, feature correlations), adapt the teacher-student relationship during training, and can be integrated with pruning or module-replacement strategies to achieve strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.
